served.stem: 2,2-Dimethylpropan-1-ol (neopentyl alcohol, shown) is treated with concentrated HBr. Which structure is the major product?
served.bankWhy: Neopentyl alcohol with HBr cannot easily do SN2 (hindered) or form a primary cation, so a 1,2-methyl shift gives a stable tertiary cation; bromide traps it to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane (option A). option B is the non-rearranged neopentyl bromide, option C a different rearranged skeleton, option D an alkene, option E the chloride. Neopentyl rearrangement is a classic textbook example.

answer.line: The tert-butyl group blocks SN2, so water leaves with a methyl sliding over, and bromide adds to the tertiary cation that results.

steps: Protonate the OH so water can leave. HBr supplies both the proton and the bromide.
Check SN2 first. The CH2 is primary, but the tert-butyl group next door blocks its back side, so bromide cannot get in.
Water leaves as a methyl shifts over with its bond pair, so no primary cation ever forms. The charge lands on a tertiary carbon, and bromide adds there.

choices.note: The skeleton did rearrange, so half of it holds. But after the shift the charge sits on the tertiary carbon, so that is where Br goes.
Losing a proton from the same tertiary cation gives this alkene, and some forms. With concentrated HBr, bromide capture wins.
A chloride needs HCl, often with ZnCl2. This flask has only HBr, and the skeleton here has not rearranged either.
Methyl shift as water leaves, then bromide on the tertiary carbon.
Primary alcohol plus HBr usually means SN2 with no shift. Neopentyl is the exception: the tert-butyl group walls off the back side.

student.lockIt: Neopentyl carbons block SN2; in acid they shift a methyl and react at the tertiary carbon.
